build: Electronic Arts disk release, two double-sided disks as four G64 side images; play copies made with the game's own Copy utility

comments.text: Ranger Center program, first instruction: JMP ranger_start. Module 3 ($CA1A) loads this file through load_program ($03AD) from track 27, logical sector 7; load_program reads the header below with the first sector, loads the pages to $7E00 and jumps through the header word ($5A03) to here.
Header, bytes 3-4 of the file's first sector: $7E00, the load and start address load_program takes from $5A03/$5A04 and jumps through. Byte 5, ranger_page_count, gives the length.

Header byte 5: $48, the page count load_program reads, 72 pages ($7E00-$C5FF). The Ranger Center is only the first 8 ($7E00-$85FF, T27/L7-L0); the other 64 are the sectors that follow on the disk (T26/L17 down to T23/L9), loaded and never used: the radio program file at $8600-$8FFF, more from $9000.

Start-up: ranger_menu_setup (the bar Create Delete Start); keeps $AB (picture shown) and $AC (picture animation flag) in saved_picture and saved_picture_anim for Start to put back; shows picture 3 from the $E000 buffer (show_picture_e000, $041C), framed and captioned with the location name at $F4D0; shows the roster (roster_show, $02B7) and opens the text window (text_window_open, $0353). Then the main loop at $7E1E: wait_key ($022F), menu_key ($02DE), for ever; menu_key runs the handlers in ranger_menu_handlers.
Main loop: wait_key ($022F), then menu_key ($02DE) with that key, which runs the handler of the item it selects; back here for ever. Only Start leaves, through load_program, which does not return.

Sets up the Ranger Center's menu: $3E/$3F = ranger_menu_text_table ($7F17), $40/$41 = ranger_menu_handler_tables ($7F19), menu 0 ($3B), item 0 (Create) selected ($39), bar on row 23 ($3D = $17), last visible item 2 ($3A: Start; hot keys 1-7 are items 3-9); then draw_menu_bar ($02E7) and highlight_menu_item ($02E1).
Menu bar text, 'Create Delete Start' and a zero: items 0-2, chosen by their first letters C, D and S, or with ',' '.' and RETURN (menu_key, $1BBF).
Hot keys of the hidden items, '1234567' and a zero: keys 1-7 run items 3-9, the handlers view_member_1 to view_member_7 in ranger_menu_handlers.

Handler table of the Ranger Center's menu, ten words: Create create_handler ($7F4E), Delete delete_handler ($83C6), Start start_handler ($7E7E), then keys 1-7: view_member_1 ($7F2A) and the six entries hidden in its BIT chain ($7F2D, $7F30, $7F33, $7F36, $7F39, $7F3C). run_menu_item ($1C55) calls the chosen word through the JSR it writes at $1C71.
$60, an RTS opcode between the handler table and start_handler that nothing reaches: no handler word, branch, jump or pointer in the program names $7E7D.

Start: with members in the current party ($07 non-zero) goes straight to start_reload_game. With an empty party and no other party ($0B = 0) it returns and the menu stays, so the game cannot be started without a member. With an empty party among several: unless it is the last ($08 = $0B), copies each later party table down one (14 bytes each, tables $08 to 3, $7E8D-$7EB6); clears table 3 (clear_party_table), lowers $0B, makes party 0 current ($08 = 0, $07 = its size, party_size_of $02AB) and takes its column, row and map from its table (+8, +9, +10 to $57, $58, $09; view corner $02/$03 = $57 - $59, $58 - $5A); then start_reload_game.
Operand of LDY #imm at $7E9F: the offset the table shift reads through ($68), set to $1B at $7E97 and lowered at $7EA7 down to $0E, so it walks the next party's 14 bytes.
Operand of LDY #imm at $7EA3: the offset the table shift writes through ($68), set to $0D at $7E9C and lowered at $7EAA; the copy stops when it passes 0 (BPL at $7EAD).

Operand of LDA #imm at $7EAF: the party whose table the shift is filling, written at $7E8F; the loop raises it from $08 and stops at 4, so table 3 receives the 14 bytes after it ($F438-$F445) before clear_party_table zeroes it.

Leaves the Ranger Center: puts $AC and $AB back from saved_picture_anim and saved_picture, saves the game state (save_game, $02D8: to the disk in the drive, no side check), waits for side 1 (check_side_1, $02D5), clears $92 (the game program tests it at its $7E5C and calls its $AE21 once when it is set) and loads the game program, track 31 logical sector 9 ($10/$11), with load_program ($03AD), which does not return.
Second entry of print_ranger_message that nothing in the program calls: X = column, Y = row of the text cursor ($23/$24), then on into $7F07 to print Ranger Center message A there.

Prints message A of the Ranger Center's packed text block, word-wrapped: $43/$44 = ranger_text ($8527), output_wrapped ($0302), print_message ($0311). Messages: 1 'You cannot create any more characters.', 2 'Create a character.', 3 'Keep this char (Y/N) ?', 4 the skill list's header, 5 'Which player do you want to delete?', 6 'Are you sure you want to delete <name>?'.
Menu text table for $3E/$3F (ranger_menu_setup): one word per menu number, a single menu here, ranger_menu_text ($7E4D).
Table of handler tables for $40/$41 (ranger_menu_setup): one word per menu number, a single menu here, ranger_menu_handlers ($7E69).

Copy of $AB, the number of the picture shown when the program started (ranger_start, $7E0B); start_reload_game puts it back ($7EE9) before the game program is loaded. 0 in play-ranger, the hand-over's $AB.

Copy of $AC, the picture animation flag when the program started (ranger_start, $7E10); start_reload_game puts it back ($7EE4). 0 in play-ranger, and animate_picture_tick ($05C5) does nothing while $AC is 0.

Zeroes the 14 bytes of party table A ($F400 + 14*A; party_table_ptr, $029F, leaves $68/$69 on it): positions 1-7, column, row, map and the rest. start_handler calls it for table 3 after moving the tables down, or at once when the empty party is the last ($7E8B).

Hot keys 1-7 (items 3-9): A = the member number; when it is at most the party size $07, the character screen of that member (view_character through $033B: sheet, P)ool and D)iv cash, items and skills pages) and then clear_window ($025C); a larger number does nothing. Key 1 enters here with LDA #$01; keys 2-7 enter inside the BIT chain at $7F2D-$7F3C.

Entry for key 2 (ranger_menu_handlers word 4): the operand bytes of BIT $02A9 at $7F2C read A9 02, LDA #$02 when entered here; the BITs after it only test memory and set flags, so the party-size test at $7F41 runs with A = 2.
Entry for key 3: LDA #$03, hidden in the operand of BIT $03A9 at $7F2F, then on through the BIT chain to the party-size test at $7F41.
Entry for key 4: LDA #$04, hidden in BIT $04A9 at $7F32.
Entry for key 5: LDA #$05, hidden in BIT $05A9 at $7F35.
Entry for key 6: LDA #$06, hidden in BIT $06A9 at $7F38.
Entry for key 7: LDA #$07, hidden in BIT $07A9 at $7F3B. The last BIT, $08A9 at $7F3E, hides an LDA #$08 that no handler word points at: '8' is not among ranger_menu_hot_keys.
Create: create_character, then clear_window ($025C) and roster_draw ($028F), so the roster shows the new member, or the party as it was when creation was refused or cancelled.

Creates a character. Counts the player characters, records 1 to $0A whose byte +$29 is 0 (an NPC's is not; with $0A = 0 record 1 is still looked at); with 4 or more prints message 1, 'You cannot create any more characters.', and returns. Otherwise raises $0A, adds the new record to the current party (party_add_current, $02A4, which does not check for room), keeps its position (find_party_of, $02B1) in new_member_position, selects it and zeroes its 256 bytes; gives it gear_kit_45 or gear_kit_9mm (random_1_to_a(2), $0242) and gear_common (give_items). Then message 2, 'Create a character.', the attributes (roll_attributes), name, sex, nationality and skills; left-arrow at those prompts, or N at the end, removes it again (cancel_creation), except in the skill list, where left-arrow shows the character sheet (skills_show_sheet).

Room for one more: $0A (characters in use) goes up by one and is the new record's number; party_add_current ($02A4) adds it to the current party, find_party_of ($02B1) leaves its position there in Y (new_member_position), select_member makes it current and its 256 bytes are zeroed ($7F99-$7F9F).

Attribute screen: four rounds (create_scratch_a = 4), each rolling ST, IQ, LK, SP, AGL, DEX and CHR (+$0E-$14) with roll_attribute and MAXCON and CON (+$1B, +$1D) as one more roll + 18 (21-36; the high bytes +$1C/+$1E stay 0), setting rank 1 (+$24), skill points = IQ (+$20) and the rank name 'Private' (+$32), and printing the block at column 14, row 3 (print_attributes, $032F, which does not use the A it is given). Then reroll_prompt_text: SPACE rolls four more rounds, RETURN accepts (enter_name), left-arrow cancels, other keys are ignored.

Cancels the creation: remove_member ($02C6) with new_member_position, so the new record goes, the records above it move down and $0A and $07 drop by one. Reached by left-arrow at the attribute, name, sex and nationality prompts, by a cancelled name input, and by N at 'Keep this char (Y/N) ?'.

Name: enter_name_text, then a line input of at most 13 characters at column 14 into $5A00 (prompt_and_input_name); left-arrow there cancels (input_line returns A = $FF). The name goes to +$00-$0D (copy_name_to_record); an empty one is asked again; check_unique_name refuses one that another record has, carry set when that second input is cancelled.
Sex: enter_sex_text, then M stores 0 and F stores 1 in +$18 (printed as Male or Female, engine messages 162 + byte); left-arrow cancels; other keys are ignored.

Nationality: nationality_menu_text, then keys 1-5 store 0-4 in +$19 (U.S., Russian, Mexican, Indian, Chinese: engine messages 145 + byte); left-arrow cancels; other keys are ignored. Goes on to skills_reset_points.

Left-arrow in the skill list: prints the character sheet (print_character_sheet, $04E4: name, attributes, sex, nationality) and the (RETURN) prompt (control code 6 through print_char_wrapped, $0284), then back to skills_screen. It does not cancel the creation.

Taken when list_choose returns $FE, the list's extra key in $BE: zeroes +$80-$BC, the 30 skill pairs and the byte after them, and gives every point back (skills_reset_points). show_skill_list puts $92 in $BE, a code the keyboard table at $C953 does not hold ('R' is $D2), so no key reaches this.
Skill points = IQ (+$20 = +$0F), then the skill list. Reached after the nationality and from skills_clear; skills already bought are not refunded here.
Skill list: clear_window ($025C) and show_skill_list (header and the first page of the skills this IQ allows), then skills_choose.

Prints 'Skill points = n' (print_skill_points) and waits for a choice (list_choose, $039B): RETURN or space go to keep_prompt, left-arrow to skills_show_sheet, $FE to skills_clear; a digit picks the skill on that line: its minimum IQ above the IQ gives not_smart_enough (impossible for a listed skill), its base cost (bits 0-2 of its skill_table byte) above the points left gives not_enough_points; otherwise buy_skill.

'Not enough skill points!' (not_enough_points_text) at column 14, row 2, direct output, then complain_pause. Reached when the base cost exceeds the points, or when the price of the next level would take them below zero.

Buys skill $49: searches the skill pairs (skill number, level) from +$80 two bytes at a time for it or for an empty pair (no limit: past +$BB it would read the items; at creation no more than 18 skills fit the points). A new skill takes the empty pair at level 1 for its base cost ($8151). A known one ($8123) costs skill_price (base cost x 2^level, 255 when that overflows) and goes up one level, unless points - price is negative (BMI at $813C, a signed test that holds while the price is under points + 129). list_flash_line ($03A1) flashes the line; then after_purchase.

The skill is known: Y (the pair's offset) goes to create_scratch_a; the price of the next level is skill_price of the base cost with X = level + 1, kept in create_scratch_b. When points - price is negative (BMI at $813C) it is refused (not_enough_points); otherwise the points drop by the price and the level rises by one ($813E-$8149); list_flash_line ($03A1), then after_purchase.

The skill is new: the empty pair (Y on its first byte) gets the skill ($49) at level 1, and the base cost (skill_base_cost, kept in create_scratch_a) comes off the points (+$20); skills_choose has already made sure they cover it. list_flash_line ($03A1), then on into after_purchase.
After a purchase: with no points left goes to keep_prompt; otherwise list_show_page ($03A4) redraws the page from its first item and skills_choose waits again.

'You are not smart enough!' (not_smart_text) at column 14, row 2, then complain_pause. Taken when the chosen skill's minimum IQ (skill_min_iq) is above the IQ, which a skill on the list cannot be: ranger_skill_row leaves those out.

After a refusal: play_sound_1 ($0232, whose sound record has the gate bit clear, so as written it starts no note), a pause of seven rounds of delay_x_times ($0237, about 1.2 seconds), then skills_choose, which prints the points over the message.

Message 3, 'Keep this char (Y/N) ?' (its code 7 reopens the text window): Y returns to create_handler with the character kept, N removes it (cancel_creation), left-arrow goes back to skills_screen; other keys are ignored.
RTS shared by give_items (the list's $FF reached, $81B3) and keep_prompt (Y, $81A2): from keep_prompt it returns from create_character to create_handler, with the character kept.

Copies an item list into the new character's item slots: items from ($14) at index create_scratch_a up to an $FF, each stored at record offset create_scratch_b with a count byte from the item's record (item_record $03C8, then item_record_byte4 $036E: the clip for a gun, 40 for Matches, 1 for a Rope, 0 for clips and most others). The list index moves on by 1 and the slot offset by 2; create_character sets the index back to 0 for the second list but not the offset, so gear_common's items follow the pistol and clips.

Refuses a name another character has: copies the new record's name (+$00-$0D) to $5A00 and compares it (strings_equal, $024F) with each record 1 to $0A in turn. The first match decides: the new character itself (party $08, position new_member_position, by find_party_of $02B1) means the name is free, carry clear; any other prints name_taken_text and asks again (prompt_and_input_name, an empty name asked once more), carry set when that input is cancelled, and the check starts over. The match is exact, and typed names are upper case, so 'HELL RAZOR' is not the pre-made 'Hell Razor'.

Not an entry: $81FA is the operand of LDA $8239 at $81F9. The symbol comes from the engine's run_menu_item JSR at $1C71, whose operand still holds $81FA, the start-up program's Start handler (its table at $81D7), the last menu item run before this program was loaded. Nothing in the Ranger Center calls $81FA.

Position (1-7) of the character being created in the current party, from find_party_of at $7F92; read by cancel_creation ($8041), by check_unique_name to recognise the record ($8211) and select it again ($8216), and at $801C as an A that print_attributes ignores. 4 in play-create and play-skills.

Scratch byte of the creation code: the record counted by create_character ($7F5E) and check_unique_name ($81DC), the list index of give_items ($81AC), the four rounds of roll_attributes ($7FDA, $8022), and in buy_skill the offset of the skill pair ($8123) or the base cost paid ($815D).

Second scratch byte: the number of player characters create_character counts ($7F59-$7F7C), the item slot offset of give_items (from $BD at $7FBD; $DB after the fifteen items, as in play-create), and the price of the next level in buy_skill ($8131).
'Private' and a zero: the rank name every new character gets, copied to its record from +$32 ($8005-$8012) and printed after 'RANK:' by print_attributes.
Gear list 1, given when random_1_to_a(2) returns 1: item $0D, the M1911A1 45 pistol (count 7 from its record: a full clip), then eight of item $1E, 45 clips; $FF ends it.
Gear list 2, given for a 2: item $10, the VP91Z 9mm pistol (count 18), then eight of item $20, 9mm clips; $FF ends it.

Gear every new character gets after the pistol and clips: items $36 Rope (count 1), $2C Canteen, $2D Crowbar, $04 Knife, $31 Hand mirror and $34 Matches (count 40); $FF ends it. Nothing equips the pistol: +$1F stays 0 (the four pre-made Rangers have 1).
'(SPACE) to roll again.' CR '(RETURN) to accept.' CR and a zero, printed word-wrapped under the attributes ($8027).
$04 (clear the window), 'Enter name ', CR, CR and a zero: the prompt of enter_name ($8047).
$04 (clear the window), $0B (the current character's name), ' is already in the game. Enter a new name.', CR, CR and a zero: check_unique_name's prompt ($821C).
$04, 'Enter sex (M/F) ', CR and a zero: the prompt of enter_sex ($8064).
$04, 'Nationality:' and the lines '1) U.S.', '2) Russian', '3) Mexican', '4) Indian', '5) Chinese', each after a CR, and a zero: the prompt of enter_nationality ($8086).
'You are not smart enough!', $03 (clear to the end of the line) and a zero, printed by not_smart_enough ($8179).
'Not enough skill points!', $03 (clear to the end of the line) and a zero, printed by not_enough_points ($8103).
Base cost in skill points of the skill whose skill_table byte $16/$17 points at: bits 0-2 of the byte (1-3 for the skills, 7 for Combat shooting). Returns Y = 0.
Minimum IQ of the skill whose skill_table byte $16/$17 points at: bits 3-7 of the byte (3-24 for the skills, 31 for Combat shooting). Returns Y = 0.

Prints the string at $31/$32 word-wrapped (print_string_wrapped, $026F), then input_line ($02EA) into $5A00, at most 13 characters ($35 = $0D), from column 14 of the cursor's row: A = 0 when RETURN ends it, $FF when left-arrow cancels. Letters come out upper case (input_line stores key codes without bit 7; F1, F3, F5 and F7 give lower-case q, s, u, w).
Copies the 14 bytes $5A00-$5A0D (the typed name and its zero; input_line clears the buffer first) to the current character's name field, +$00-$0D.

One attribute roll: five roll_d6 ($023A) into roll_dice, an exchange loop meant to move the larger dice up, then A = the sum of slots 4, 3 and 2 (3-18); Y is kept (roll_saved_y_op). After an exchange the loop goes on comparing the die it started with (BPL at $83AB goes back to the CMP, not to the LDA at $8397), so a later exchange overwrites the die just moved up and the small one is copied twice: the sum is not the best three of five. Over all 7,776 throws the mean is 10.62 (best three of five 13.43, 3d6 10.5); 3 comes once, 18 81 times (1.0 %), 4 and 5 3.3 % and 3.4 % of the time against 1.4 % and 2.8 % for 3d6.

Operand of LDY #imm at $83BE: the caller's Y, stored at $8382 and given back as roll_attribute returns: the record offset roll_attributes is filling, $0E-$14, or $15 for the MAXCON roll ($15 in play-create).
The five dice of roll_attribute, slots 0-4, filled from slot 4 down; the sum takes slots 2-4. 1 1 1 1 3 in play-create, the MAXCON roll: 3 + 1 + 1 = 5, MAXCON 23.
Delete: delete_member, then clear_window ($025C) and roster_draw ($028F).

Deletes a member: nothing when the party is empty ($07 = 0). Message 5, 'Which player do you want to delete?', then pick_member ($02AE: keys 1 to the party size; left-arrow gives 0 and returns); selects the member and asks message 6, 'Are you sure you want to delete <name>?': Y removes it (remove_member, $02C6: the record goes, later ones move down), any other key returns. No check of +$29: an NPC can be deleted too, and so can the party's only member.
Y pressed: remove_member ($02C6) with the position kept in delete_position; its RTS returns to delete_handler.
The position (1-7) picked for deletion, kept from pick_member ($83DF) for remove_member ($83F2). 4 in play-create and play-skills: the fourth Ranger was deleted before them (orientation.md).

Shows the skill list: message 4 (clears the window; header '   IQ PTS LVL   SKILL'); $BE = $92 (the list's extra key, a code no key produces); first item and choice 1 ($4A, $49); per-line routine $47/$48 = ranger_skill_row ($8468); counts into $4E the skills 1-36 whose minimum IQ (skill_min_iq) is at most the IQ (+$0F), keeping the last of them in $D1, which list_line_label marks with '_' instead of '>'; $4D = $24, so the list offers skills 1-35; first row 4 ($42), 9 lines ($4F); then list_show_page ($03A4).

Prints 'Skill points = ' (skill_points_text, which clears to the end of the line) at column 14, row 2 with direct output, then A in decimal (print_byte, $02F6, which sets its own width: the $30 = 2 stored before it has no effect).
'Skill points = ', $03 (clear to the end of the line) and a zero, printed by print_skill_points.

Per-line routine of the skill list (list_show_page calls it through $47/$48 with A = the skill): carry set and nothing printed when the skill's minimum IQ is above the IQ (+$0F). Otherwise list_line_label ($03A7: the line's digit and '>', or '_' on the last skill the IQ allows, which show_skill_list keeps in $D1), then, with $43/$44 on the engine's text block (the word at $0200, $29E4): the minimum IQ in two columns, the price of the next level in three (skill_price of the base cost and the character's level from skill_level, $0359), the level in three, and the skill's name (engine message n, print_message $0311); carry clear.
Operand of LDA #imm at $84A9: the skill's base cost, written at $849B and handed to skill_price for the PTS column.
Operand of LDA #imm at $84B5: the character's level in the skill (skill_level, written at $84A4), printed in the LVL column.
The skill ranger_skill_row is printing (A on entry, stored at $8468), kept for the second point_at_skill, skill_level and the name. 9 in play-skills, the last line drawn (Perception).

Price of the next level: A = base cost, X = level + 1; returns A = cost x 2^level, or 255 when 2^level or the product passes 255. 2^level is built by shifting, kept in price_step_op and added cost - 1 more times. The skill list prints it and buy_skill charges it.
Operand of LDA #imm at $84D7: 2^level, written at $84D2; the first term of the price, and the amount skill_price adds for each further unit of cost (ADC $84D8 at $84DE).

Points $16/$17 at skill A's byte in skill_table ($8502 + A) and makes record_address's table the same ($45/$46 = $8502, record size $4C = 1), so list_choose's choice can be looked up with record_address ($039E) at $80E7.

Skills the Ranger Center sells, one byte per skill at $8502 + n (byte 0 unused): bits 3-7 the minimum IQ, bits 0-2 the base cost. Skills 1-7 (Brawling to Swim) IQ 3; 8-9 IQ 6; 10-12 IQ 9; 13-16 IQ 10; 17 Combat shooting $FF, IQ 31 and cost 7, so never offered (a rolled IQ is at most 18); 18 IQ 11; 19 IQ 12; 20-21 IQ 13; 22-23 IQ 14; all those cost 1. 24-26 IQ 15, 27 IQ 16, 28 IQ 17, cost 2; 29 IQ 19, 30-31 IQ 20, 32 IQ 21, 33 IQ 22, 34 IQ 23, 35 IQ 24, cost 3, out of reach at creation. Names: engine messages 1-35.

$EA, the byte after skill 35: show_skill_list's counting loop reads it as a skill 36 (minimum IQ 29, cost 2) and never counts it, since a rolled IQ does not reach 29; the list itself stops at 35 ($4D = $24). The radio file also has an $EA just before its text block (radio $82D8).

Packed text block of the Ranger Center (base for $43/$44, print_ranger_message): the 60-byte alphabet. Codes 0-$1D: ' eatroc', CR, 'yl', the end code ($0A, whose entry is $00), 'nhusiwpd?', $04, 'k.', $07, 'vqm/)('; entries $1E and $1F, reached through the escape code $1F followed by 0 or 1, are $0B and $06; the 28 entries after them are $7F, unused.

Word table of ranger_text (base + $3C), offsets from $8563: group 0 (messages 0-3) at +$06 = $8569, group 1 (messages 4-7) at +$43 = $85A6. The third word, $E0A4, is no valid offset, and no message the program prints (1-6) needs it.

Messages 0-3 of ranger_text, one bit stream: 0 empty; 1 $04 'You cannot create any more characters.' CR $06 (create_character); 2 $07 'Create a character.' CR (create_character); 3 $07 'Keep this char (Y/N) ?' CR (keep_prompt). The stream ends with the last bit of $85A4; $85A5 ($48), before group 1, is not read.

Messages 4-6 of ranger_text: 4 $04 CR '   IQ PTS LVL   SKILL' CR (show_skill_list); 5 $04 'Which player do you want to delete?' CR and 6 CR CR 'Are you sure you want to delete ' $0B '?' CR (delete_member). Message 6 ends in bit 0 of $85EF; there is no message 7.

The last 16 bytes of the Ranger Center's last sector (T27/L0), after its text; nothing reads them. $85F1-$85FF are the game program's (T31/L9) bytes at the same addresses (the end of its BNE $8653, STX $8600, LDA #$FF, STA $872B,X, JSR $8606, BCC $8652, LDX #), probably memory left from the game program when this file was made; $85F0 ($83) matches no snapshot.

From here to $8FFF: the radio program's file ('Radio and promotion', T26/L17, 10 pages), byte for byte, read by this program's 72-page load because it follows T27/L0 on the disk (the whole load is described at $9000, filler_sectors_t26_l7_l6). It is assembled for $7E00 (radio address = this address - $800) and never runs here: no instruction, menu word or pointer of the Ranger Center reaches $8600-$8FFF, and its own calls would land in the Ranger Center (its JSR $7E4F at $8616 in ranger_menu_text). This stretch is radio $7E00-$7EA2: JMP $7EA3, the header ($7E00, 10 pages), a six-note tune at radio $7E06 (frequency and length tables $7E34-$7E45, delay loop $7E46) and the SID writer at $7E4F with its register bytes ($7E98-$7EA2).

Copy of radio $7EA3-$80C1: the code its JMP $7EA3 starts (stack reset, roster, the caption 'Ranger Ctr.' copied from radio $8184 to $F4D0, portrait 8, then a pass over the characters that gives the Base Cochise reward, radio $7EBC, and a pass that promotes them, radio $7F0B) and its routine for distributing attribute points (radio $801C-$80C1). What it does is the radio part's to describe; never run here.

Copy of radio $80C2-$818F: the keys 1-8 as key codes ($B1-$B8) and a zero; the strings $04 $0B ' has ' $0F ' point' $0A $0A 's' $0A ' to distribute.' CR CR 'Choose an attribute:' CR '1) Strength  :', then CR '2) IQ/Skill  :' to CR '8) Maxcon    :', each ending in a zero; $08 and a zero; and 'Ranger Ctr.' and a zero (radio $8184-$818F), the name the radio copies to $F4D0.

Copy of radio $8190-$81D7: the radio's exit, which its JMP $8190 at radio $8013 reaches (clears $AC and $92, waits for side 1, loads the game program, T31/L9, with load_program), and its message helpers: radio $81A4 and $81A8 print radio message A word-wrapped, $81B3 sets the text base $82D9, and $81BC decodes a message into the record from +$32, the rank name. Never run here.

Copy of radio $81D8-$82D8: a 256-byte table, one byte per rank 0-255, giving the radio message that names the rank (1 'Private' for ranks 0 and 1, rising to 50 'General Argent' at rank 131; above that 50, except 51-55 at ranks 141, 151 ... 231 and 251-255), and the $EA before the radio's text block. The radio reads it at its $7FC9 and $7FCE.

Copy of the radio's packed text block (radio base $82D9, the base the copy of the radio's code at $89B3 would set): alphabet, a 17-word group table (the last word, $9AA3, invalid) and messages 0-55, the rank names 'Private', 'Private 1st class' ... 'Revenant Argent', 'Supreme Jerk'. Not the Ranger Center's text: that is ranger_text.

Copy of the radio's messages 56-62 (radio $857D-$8748): '<name> has achieved the rank of', '<name> is still a', 'You get n adventure point(s) to distribute among your stats.', '... doesn't have quite enough experience to be considered for', 'another', the 'Congratulations Rangers on a mission well done.' speech about Base Cochise, and 'promotion.'; the text ends at $8F48.

Copy of radio $8749-$87FF, the radio file's last bytes after its text. From radio $874B on they equal the game program's bytes at the same addresses (part of its code from $874D), except two operands, $BB71 and $BAE2 where the game program has $BB75 and $BAE6: apparently memory left from another build of the game program when the radio file was written, as the Ranger Center's own $85F1-$85FF are. Never run here. The Ranger Center's load goes on at $9000 with T26/L7.

From here to $C5FF: disk sectors the Ranger Center's load sweeps in after its own file and the radio program ($8600-$8FFF). The program's header asks for 72 pages ($7E05 = $48), so load_program ($2890) reads T27/L7 and the 71 logical sectors after it to $7E00-$C5FF; the program itself is only T27/L7-L0 ($7E00-$85FF), and $8600-$C5FF is side 1 from T26/L17 (the radio program) down to T23/L9, byte for byte (read from the disk image with the loader's own stepping, the 72 sectors equal the hand-over). These two, T26/L7 and T26/L6, hold no file's data: $4B, then 255 bytes of $01, the filler of 146 sectors of side 1, among them all of tracks 2, 3, 6 and 7 and every sector the loader's stepping passes over (T24/L18, T30/L17, track 17's L1-L20). Nothing reads $9000-$C5FF while the Ranger Center runs: its code ($7E00-$8501, traced from $7E00, the handler table $7E69 and the list routine $8468) names no address above $84EA and points nowhere past $85EF; of the 5,562 instructions of the engine's code and this program's (4,900 and 662), only two name an address here: the loader's store at $FF34, which wrote the load, and the picture reader at $06C4, left at $A211, inside the title picture's buffer ($B9/$BA = $8A00), with the animation off ($AC = 0), and moved into $E000 when the Ranger Center shows its portrait ($7E15); and the range is the same in play-ranger, play-create and play-skills as at the hand-over. Start loads the game (T31/L9) over all of it.

Side 1's T26/L5-L3, swept in by the 72-page load (see $9000): item table file 0, entry 0 of the directory T35/L15, the file load_item_table ($26BD) reads to $3100. Byte for byte the table at $3100-$33FF in every Ranger Center snapshot and in the game's play-map: an 8-byte header ($60 $60 $60 $00 $37 $08 $F8 $39), then 95 eight-byte item records, item n at $9208 + 8n, in the layout the engine reads at $3108 + 8n (byte 3 the class and use effect, 4 the clip size or uses, 5 the skill, 6 the damage dice or armour class). This copy is never read: the Ranger Center's starting gear ($81AC) looks its items up at $3108 + 8n through $03C8.

Side 1's T26/L2-L0, swept in by the 72-page load (see $9000): item table file 1, entry 1 of T35/L15, the other item table on side 1. The same 768 bytes as file 0 at $9200 except byte 2 of three records: Engine (item 46, $967A) is $00 here and $FF in file 0; Shovel (55, $96C2) and Snake squeezin (57, $96D2) are $FF here and $00 there. Apart from those, byte 2 is $FF in both files for items 43-56 (Book to Sledge hammer) and 91-93 (Clay pot, Fruit, Jewelry), 17 in record 94 (Cash) and 0 in the rest; what the game does with byte 2 is the item table owner's to settle. Nothing reads this copy.

Side 1's T25/L17 and T25/L16, swept in by the 72-page load (see $9000): two more sectors of filler, $4B and 255 bytes of $01 each as at $9000, between side 1's item table files (T26/L5-L0, $9200-$97FF) and its module area, which starts at T25/L15 ($9A00). Nothing reads them.

Module 0's packed stream, swept in by the 72-page load (see $9000): entry 0 of the module directory T34/L16, on all four sides; side 1's copy opens the module area at T25/L15, the base in that directory sector's last two bytes. $9A00-$9D98, 921 bytes. The unpacker (T35/L16, run at $C800) takes a 20-byte value table first ($9A00-$9A13, to $F4E5-$F4F8), then codes, most significant bit first: 0 + 8 bits, a literal; 1 + a prefix code for one of the 20 values (000-001 values 0-1, 0100-1010 values 2-8, 10110-11101 values 9-16, 111100-111110 values 17-19); 1 + 111111 + a count byte + a value, a run. These bytes decode to module 0's 999 bytes, $CA00-$CDE6, the same from all four sides. The entry's third byte, 4, counted down in $CE for every 256 bytes read, makes the unpacker read 1,024 bytes, through the first 103 of the stream that follows (module 1's on sides 1, 2 and 4, here $9D99-$9DFF; module 2's on side 3), so it writes more bytes that depend on the side: 109 ($CDE7-$CE53) from sides 1, 2 and 4, 117 ($CDE7-$CE5B) from side 3. load_module ($2691) unpacks it from the disk; this copy is never read.

Module 1's packed stream, swept in by the 72-page load (see $9000): entry 1 of T34/L16 (sides 1, 2 and 4), right after module 0's: $9D99-$A14B, 947 bytes, in module 0's format (see $9A00), value table $9D99-$9DAC (20 03 A9 85 CC 02 CD 00 F0 C9 B1 A0 4C D0 60 FF 48 16 01 8D). Up to $9FFF it decodes to $CA00-$CCBA; the rest is under $A000. Its bytes give module 1's 1,061 bytes ($CA00-$CE24), the same from all three sides; the 1,024-byte window runs on through module 3's stream ($A14C-$A17C) and the zero bytes after it, to $A198, and writes 84 more bytes ($CE25-$CE78, the last 24 of them zeros from those zero bytes); from sides 2 and 4 the window writes 85 other bytes ($CE25-$CE79). load_module unpacks it from the disk; this copy is never read.

Module 1's packed stream continued from $9D99 (a second label because a data span stops at $A000): $A000-$A14B, the codes that decode to module 1's $CCBB-$CE24, the last of what its own bytes give. load_module unpacks it from side 1's T25/L9-L8, or from side 2 or 4, never from this copy.

Module 3's packed stream, swept in by the 72-page load (see $9000): entry 3 of T34/L16, on side 1 only, $A14C-$A17C, 49 bytes (value table $A14C-$A15F, then codes). They decode to module 3's 37 bytes of code, $CA00-$CA24, the routine that brings up the Ranger Center: JSR $03B9 (save_map), JSR $02D8 (save_game), the 12-byte place name from ($5F)+3 to $F4D0 ('Ranger Ctr.' in play-ranger), wait for side 1 ($02D5), then $10/$11 = 27/7 and JMP $03AD, which loads this program. Its count byte, 1, makes the unpacker read 256 bytes, to $A24B, through the 129 zero bytes after it, the sector's last two ($19 $11) and the first 76 of tile set 0, so it writes $CA25-$CB7C too: zeros to $CA97, then bytes decoded from $A1FE on. This copy is never read.

End of side 1's module area, swept in by the 72-page load (see $9000): the rest of sector T25/L8 after module 3's stream, 129 zero bytes ($A17D-$A1FD), then $19 $11 (25, 17) in the sector's last two bytes, whose purpose is not known: the engine reads a sector's last bytes only in the side check ($18B2, $18B9: T35/L8) and for a stream directory's base ($276F, $2772), never in this sector. The unpacker reads these bytes only as the tails of read windows: module 3's 256-byte window takes them all, the zeros coming out as zeros ($CA25-$CA97), and module 1's 1,024-byte window on side 1 takes the first 28, to $A198 (zeros at $CE61-$CE78). The tile sets start on the next sector, T25/L7 ($A200).

Tile set 0's packed stream, swept in by the 72-page load (see $9000): entry 0 of the tile-set directory T35/L12, side 1, at its base T25/L7; the world map's tile set: of 42 maps snapshotted as enter_map returned, only map 0 has header byte $30 (read through $61/$62 at $25EE) = 0, and its $D000-$DD7F then equals this stream's decode. $A200-$AB07, 2,312 bytes, in module 0's format (see $9A00), value table 00 10 04 40 01 AA 44 30 80 11 41 6A FF 9A AB A6 06 02 F0 B0; $A200-$A5FF decode to $D000-$D605. unpack_tile_set ($2722) unpacks it from the disk to $D000: its own bytes give exactly the 3,456 bytes $D000-$DD7F, then the decode reads tile set 1's first 124 bytes (to $AB83) into $DD80-$DDFF, which the engine puts back from the stack. This copy is never read.

Tile set 0's packed stream continued from $A200 (a label every 1,024 bytes): $A600-$A9FF, side 1's T25/L3-L0, the codes that decode to $D606-$DBAC of the world map's tile set. Unpacked from the disk by unpack_tile_set, never from this copy.

The end of tile set 0's packed stream, $AA00-$AB07 (side 1's T24/L17 and the first 8 bytes of T24/L16, the loader taking T24/L17 after T25/L0), decoding to $DBAD-$DD7F, the last of the world map's tile set; tile set 1's stream follows at once at $AB08. Never read in the Ranger Center.

Tile set 1's packed stream, swept in by the 72-page load (see $9000): entry 1 of T35/L12, side 1, nine sectors on from the base and 8 bytes in; the tile set of maps 8, 9, 10, 29, 43 and 49, the maps of those 42 (see $A200) whose header byte $30 is 1, each then holding exactly this stream's decode at $D000-$DD7F. $AB08-$B462, 2,395 bytes, in module 0's format (see $9A00), value table 00 55 AA 10 40 56 01 65 59 44 50 04 15 54 95 80 05 20 45 11; $AB08-$AEFF decode to $D000-$D543. Its own bytes give the 3,456 bytes $D000-$DD7F; the decode then reads the zero bytes after it to $B4F2, writing zeros to $DD80-$DDFF, which unpack_tile_set ($2722) puts back from the stack. This copy is never read.

Tile set 1's packed stream continued from $AB08 (a label every 1,024 bytes): $AF00-$B2FF, side 1's T24/L12-L9, the codes that decode to $D544-$DAC5 of the tile set of maps 8, 9, 10, 29, 43 and 49. Unpacked from the disk, never from this copy.

The end of tile set 1's packed stream, $B300-$B462, decoding to $DAC6-$DD7F; $B462 is the last non-zero byte of side 1's tile-set area, and the byte whose bits complete $DD7F. Never read in the Ranger Center.

End of side 1's tile-set area, swept in by the 72-page load (see $9000): the rest of sector T24/L7 after tile set 1's stream, 157 zero bytes ($B463-$B4FF). The unpacker reads them up to $B4F2 as the tail of tile set 1's window and writes zeros to $DD80-$DDFF, which unpack_tile_set then puts back from the stack; nothing else reads them. The portraits start on the next sector, T24/L6 ($B500).

Portrait 0's packed stream, swept in by the 72-page load (see $9000): entry 0 of the portrait directory T35/L10, on all four sides; side 1's copy opens the portrait area at its base T24/L6. $B500-$B828, 809 bytes, in module 0's format (see $9A00). load_portrait ($2631) unpacks it from the disk to $CA00 or $E000; its own bytes give 965 bytes, the same from every side: header 01 10 0B 63 (columns 1-11, pixel rows 16-99, the picture window), base frame at +$54, animation scripts at +$0E, +$1B, +$3D and +$4A (start_picture $0586). The four-block window then decodes the first bytes of the next stream as well: portrait 1's on sides 1, 2 and 4, portrait 2's on side 3. This copy is never read.

Portrait 1's packed stream, swept in by the 72-page load (see $9000): entry 1 of T35/L10 (sides 1, 2 and 4), right after portrait 0's: $B829-$BB63, 827 bytes, decoding to 1,031 bytes, the same from the three sides: columns 1-11, pixel rows 16-99, base frame at +$54, scripts at +$0E, +$1B, +$3A and +$4A. Unpacked from the disk by load_portrait; this copy is never read.

Portrait 3's packed stream, swept in by the 72-page load (see $9000): entry 3 of T35/L10, side 1 only, $BB64-$BED2, 879 bytes, decoding to 1,078 bytes: columns 1-11, pixel rows 16-99, base frame at +$2D, one animation script at +$0E. The Ranger Center's own picture: its code shows portrait 3 ($7E13, show_picture_e000), and the picture at $E000 in play-ranger equals this stream's decode byte for byte. The engine unpacks it from the disk all the same (T24/L0 from byte $64); this copy is never read.

Portrait 6's packed stream, swept in by the 72-page load (see $9000): entry 6 of T35/L10, side 1 only, $BED3-$C25F, 909 bytes, value table 00 22 80 88 06 02 01 20 08 AA 05 04 8A 40 C0 2A 11 A2 55 44. Its bytes give 1,160 bytes: columns 1-11, pixel rows 16-99, base frame at +$38, scripts at +$0E, +$1B and +$2E; up to $BFFF they decode to $E000-$E17A. Unpacked from the disk by load_portrait; this copy is never read.
Portrait 6's packed stream continued from $BED3 (a second label because a data span stops at $C000): $C000-$C25F, decoding to $E17B-$E487, the end of portrait 6. Never read in the Ranger Center.

Portrait 8's packed stream, swept in by the 72-page load (see $9000): entry 8 of T35/L10, on all four sides, $C260-$C5D1, 882 bytes, decoding to 1,092 bytes: columns 1-11, pixel rows 16-99, base frame at +$43, scripts at +$0E and +$27. Unpacked from the disk by load_portrait; this copy is never read.

The first 46 bytes of portrait 10's packed stream (entry 10 of T35/L10, side 1; byte $D2 of T23/L9, sixteen sectors on from the portrait base): the 72-page load ends at $C5FF, so the other 902 of its 948 bytes stay on the disk (T23/L8 on). From the disk it decodes to 1,172 bytes: columns 1-11, pixel rows 16-99, base frame at +$30, one script at +$0E. Never read here.
